title: Edge0-145B: Frontier AI Capabilities on Your Own Computer
lede: Edge0 open-sourced Edge0-145B, a 145B-parameter mixture-of-experts model built to run on a laptop, with about 10B parameters active per step and a reported 29 GB peak memory.

points: Groups of 64 experts share two large matrices, with small per-expert parameters capturing their differences.
Hot experts stay in GPU memory, about 40 GB of experts sit in system RAM, and vocabulary data is read from SSD on demand.
CPU and GPU split the work, and speculative decoding helps reach a reported 80+ tokens per second.
Edge0's own evaluations put it at 64.6 on DeepSWE 1.1 and 90.4 on GPQA-Diamond.
The weights, a smaller Edge0-120B and the inference framework are released together.

points.text: Several suspect a rebranded Qwen3.8-Flash-Next; a reply notes the Hugging Face page lists it as the base model.
The shared-matrix design draws praise for fitting 145B parameters in about 29 GB, though a reply finds no guide to actually run it.
Hardware support is contested: one says the NVFP4 release is Blackwell-only, a reply points to a q3k build and Mac benchmarks.
One asks whether ordinary users own laptops able to run it at all.
